resources.string: Shows a mouse cursor and taps the screen for the TVBox Remote app on your phone. The service listens only on your local network. A phone must pair with a code that the TV shows. The service does not read the screen content.
Use your phone as a mouse for this TV box.
Status: off. Turn on the accessibility service.
Status: on. Address %1$s, port %2$d. Connected phones: %3$d.
The paired phones are removed. Each phone must pair again.
This box has no accessibility settings screen. Use the ADB command below.
How to turn on the receiver

1. Select "Open accessibility settings".
2. Select "TVBox Remote mouse" and turn it on.
3. On the phone, open TVBox Remote and open the mouse screen. The phone finds this box.
4. The TV shows a 4-digit code. Type the code on the phone.

Android 13 and later: if the switch is gray, open Settings, then Apps, then TVBox Remote Receiver. Open the menu of the app info screen and select "Allow restricted settings". Then do step 2 again.

If the box has no accessibility settings, connect a computer with ADB and type:
adb shell settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services com.tvboxremote.receiver/.CursorAccessibilityService
Security: the receiver works only on your local network. Its traffic is not encrypted. Use it only on a home network that you trust.
